statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 13 sits in the low band while Stress 53 sits in the elevated band.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold across all 24 published hours. The 14:00-16:00 UTC span covering post-open price discovery, the Dallas Fed release and the European cash close is flagged as the window where conditional risk is concentrated. The mapped state stays EA_ON for the whole horizon, and the assessment applies jointly to NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD.
headline: Nasdaq-100 drifts toward session lows an hour into the US cash open while NVDA and semiconductors stay green, Brent holds above $90 and September Fed hike odds top 60%
body: About an hour into the final August US cash session the Nasdaq-100 index trades near 29,316, down about 0.40% from a 29,433 previous close, close to its cash-session low of 29,306 and inside a cash range of 29,306-29,465. NQ futures near 29,409 are down about 0.28% and sit roughly 135 points above the low of a 29,274.75-29,545.50 overnight range that is now unchanged across a sixth consecutive hourly assessment. Neither futures extreme has been retested. The decline is broad but shallow: the S&P 500 is off about 0.57%, the Dow about 0.80% and the Russell 2000 about 0.72%. The important internal detail is that it is not one-way at index level. NVDA trades near 219.61, up 0.95%, and the VanEck semiconductor ETF is up about 0.38%, so AI and semiconductor leadership is firm while rate- and energy-sensitive parts of the tape carry the weakness. One semiconductor ETF quote read materially lower than these, conflicted with two independent instrument-level reads, and was discarded rather than used. Cross-asset inputs are aligned in the risk-negative direction without being extreme. Brent trades near $90.67, up 2.92%, and WTI near $85.69, up 2.74%, after US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers near the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday and Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they targeted US bases in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates. The 10-year Treasury yield is near 4.763%, up about four basis points, and the 30-year near 5.26%. Market-implied odds of a 25 basis point Federal Reserve hike in September have moved above 60% from 41.4% a week earlier, following Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks that inflation remains above target. VIX is 15.37, up 6.51% from a 14.43 close but still a historically ordinary absolute level. Tail is set at 13. Multiple amplifiers are genuinely present - aligned oil, yields, hawkish repricing and geopolitical escalation - but the pathological price path that Tail measures requires observed persistent directional efficiency, and the tape is not delivering it: the futures range is unchanged, neither extreme has been retested, megacap and semiconductor leadership is green against a red index, and implied volatility is low in absolute terms. Conflicting internals of this kind belong in Stress rather than Tail. Stress is set at 53 in the elevated band on the volatility uptick, the energy shock, the live rate-hike debate and month-end rebalancing into the 20:00 UTC close. Confidence is 86, supported by current verified index, futures, volatility, yield and oil levels, an observed post-open price path, a verified seven-day calendar and cross-checked leadership data. The shared Finviz context file was approximately seven hours old at run time and was therefore treated as stale and not used. Dominant mode is mixed. The Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index for August is scheduled at 14:30 UTC and had not printed at the assessment cutoff.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments were available and every one mapped to EA_ON. Tail held at 5 through the Sunday US afternoon and reopen window, stepped to 9 at 22:00 UTC and 14-15 across 23:00-00:00 UTC as the Iran escalation was first priced, then decayed back to 5 by 07:00-08:00 UTC. It spiked to the window peak of 17 at 09:00 UTC as oil extended, eased through 11, 10 and 9 over the next three hours, and ticked to 12 at 13:00 UTC around the US cash open. Stress rose from 26 to 52, dipped to 47 and returned to 52. Dominant mode ran normal through the Sunday session, turned mixed after 23:00 UTC with one trend-down hour at 00:00 UTC and two event/whipsaw hours at 09:00 and 10:00 UTC. The shape of the window is an event shock that was absorbed and repeatedly retraced rather than extended.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook keeps the mapped state at EA_ON for all 24 hours, with conditional Tail never leaving the low band. It runs 13 in the current hour, steps to 15 for the 15:00 UTC European cash close, eases to 12-13 through the quiet US afternoon, then rises to 15 and a horizon peak of 16 for the 19:00 and 20:00 UTC month-end rebalancing and cash-close hours, the only slot carried as event/whipsaw. It falls back to 12 after the close and settles to an 8-10 overnight baseline across the Asian session, where three hours are carried as normal. From the European pre-open it builds gradually through 9, 10, 11 and 12 as liquidity and the September 1 data block approach, closing the horizon at 15 for the 13:00 UTC hour containing the September 1 US cash open, the Barr speech and the S&P Global PMI final. Stress peaks at 55 into the month-end close, decays to 37-40 overnight and rebuilds to 50 by the end of the horizon. Confidence declines from 86 to 57 purely with forecast distance.
